https://github.com/calcom/cal.com/pull/8.pr_title: Async import of the appStore packages

golden_comments.comment: Consider adding try-catch around the await to handle import failures gracefully

The code uses forEach with async callbacks, which causes asynchronous operations (e.g., calendar/video event deletions, payment refunds) to run concurrently without being awaited. This 'fire-and-forget' behavior leads to unhandled promise rejections, race conditions, and incomplete cleanup, as surrounding try-catch blocks cannot properly handle errors from these unawaited promises. Replace forEach with for...of loops or Promise.all() with map() to ensure proper sequential execution and error handling.

The forEach callback is async but forEach does not await promises. This means calendar.deleteEvent and deleteMeeting calls are never awaited, so deletions may not complete. Errors are silently swallowed. This affects the reschedule flow for Vital app bookings.

In handleCancelBooking, a forEach loop with async callback iterates over calendar credentials. The calendar.updateEvent calls inside the nested for loop are never awaited, so recurring event updates during cancellation may not persist.

handleCancelBooking calls getCalendar (which now does a dynamic import) multiple times in sequence: once for each booking reference in the cancellation loop, and again for calendar credentials in the recurring event update section. Each call triggers a dynamic import of the calendar app module. Previously these were synchronous property lookups.

getVideoAdapters now uses a for-await loop to dynamically import each video app module sequentially. Previously all modules were statically imported at startup. If a user has multiple video credentials (e.g., Zoom, Google Meet, Daily), each video operation (create/update/delete meeting, get availability) now incurs sequential dynamic import overhead. This affects createMeeting, updateMeeting, deleteMeeting, getBusyVideoTimes, and all Daily video operations.

[Medium] Repeated dynamic imports in getCalendarCredentials add latency to calendar operations

getCalendarCredentials calls getCalendar for each credential, which now triggers a dynamic import per credential. This function is called during getConnectedCalendars, getCachedResults, createEvent, updateEvent, and deleteEvent. Each call now incurs dynamic import overhead.

golden_comments.comment: The exported function TwoFactor handles backup codes and is in BackupCode.tsx. Inconsistent naming.
Error message mentions 'backup code login' but this is a disable endpoint, not login

Backup code validation is case-sensitive due to the use of indexOf(). This causes validation to fail if a user enters uppercase hex characters, as backup codes should be case-insensitive for a better user experience.

Because backupCodes are decrypted and mutated in memory before being written back, two concurrent login requests using the same backupCode could both pass this check and update, so a single backup code may effectively be accepted more than once if used concurrently, weakening the intended one-time-use semantics.

[Medium] Race condition in backup code consumption during login

When a backup code is used during login, the code is verified and then consumed by setting it to null in the array and re-encrypting. However, there is no atomic operation or database-level locking. If two login requests arrive simultaneously with the same backup code, both could pass the indexOf check before either updates the database, allowing the same backup code to be used twice.

[High] Interface break: TwoFactorAuthAPI.disable called with 2 arguments instead of 3

The file `apps/web/components/security/DisableTwoFactorModal.tsx` (line 30) calls `TwoFactorAuthAPI.disable(password, totpCode)` with only 2 arguments. The function signature was changed in this PR to accept 3 arguments: `disable(password: string, code: string, backupCode: string)`. The third argument `backupCode` is now required. This caller was not updated, so it will pass `undefined` for `backupCode`. The API endpoint will receive `backupCode: undefined` (omitted from JSON), causing the backup code branch to be skipped. If the user has 2FA enabled and provides a valid TOTP code, the disable will still work via the TOTP path. However, if the user tries to use a backup code from this component (which doesn't have the backup code UI), it will fail. More critically, TypeScript strict mode would flag this as a type error since the third parameter is not optional.

https://github.com/calcom/cal.com/pull/1.pr_title: fix: handle collective multiple host on destinationCalendar

golden_comments.comment: Potential null reference if mainHostDestinationCalendar is undefined if evt.destinationCalendar is null or an empty array
The optional chaining on mainHostDestinationCalendar?.integration is redundant since you already check mainHostDestinationCalendar in the ternary condition.

Logic error: when externalCalendarId is provided, you're searching for a calendar where externalId === externalCalendarId, but this will always fail since you're looking for a calendar that matches itself. Should likely find by credentialId or use different logic.

Logic inversion in organization creation: The slug property is now conditionally set when IS_TEAM_BILLING_ENABLED is true, instead of when it's false as originally intended. This change, combined with requestedSlug still being set when IS_TEAM_BILLING_ENABLED is true, results in both properties being set when billing is enabled, and neither when disabled

The Calendar interface now requires createEvent(event, credentialId), but some implementations (e.g., Lark/Office365) still declare createEvent(event) only—this breaks the interface contract (also applies to other locations in the PR).

review_comments.body:
[Medium] N+1 calendar event creation for team bookings with multiple destination calendars

The `createAllCalendarEvents` method now iterates over all destination calendars in the array (one per team member for collective events). Previously, `destinationCalendar` was a single object, so the loop ran at most once. Now for a team event with N members, it runs N times, each potentially making a DB query to fetch credentials and an external API call to create the calendar event. This adds N-1 extra external API calls per booking creation for team events.

[Medium] Missing authorization check when fetching credentials by ID from database

In `createAllCalendarEvents` and `updateAllCalendarEvents`, when a credential is not found in memory (`this.calendarCredentials`), the code fetches it directly from the database using `prisma.credential.findUnique` without verifying that the current user or team has access to that credential. The `destinationCalendar` array (now supporting multiple entries) contains `credentialId` values that could potentially be manipulated by an attacker if they can influence the booking data. An attacker who can control the `destinationCalendar` entries could specify arbitrary `credentialId` values, causing the system to fetch and use credentials belonging to other users, leading to unauthorized calendar access.

[Medium] N+1 database query in createAllCalendarEvents when credentials not cached

When processing multiple destination calendars, if a credential is not found in the in-memory cache (this.calendarCredentials), the code makes a database query (prisma.credential.findUnique) for each destination. This creates an N+1 query pattern where N is the number of destination calendars. For team events with multiple hosts (each with their own destination calendar), this could result in 5-10+ additional DB queries per booking creation.

[Medium] N+1 database query in updateAllCalendarEvents when credentials not cached

Similar to createAllCalendarEvents, when updating calendar events, if a credential is not found in the in-memory cache, the code makes a database query for each calendar reference. This creates an N+1 query pattern where N is the number of calendar references. For events with multiple references (e.g., collective hosts), this could result in multiple additional DB queries per booking update.

[High] Potential null dereference when destinationCalendar is empty or undefined

When `evt.destinationCalendar` is an empty array or undefined, `mainHostDestinationCalendar` will be undefined. Accessing `.integration` on undefined will throw a TypeError at runtime. This can happen when creating an event without a destination calendar set.

[High] Null pointer access when destinationCalendar is empty array

In the `create` method of EventManager, the code destructures `evt.destinationCalendar ?? []` to get `mainHostDestinationCalendar`. If `destinationCalendar` is an empty array `[]` (which can now happen due to the change in `handleCancelBooking.ts` that returns `[]` instead of `undefined`), then `mainHostDestinationCalendar` will be `undefined`. The subsequent access `mainHostDestinationCalendar.integration` will throw a TypeError: Cannot read properties of undefined (reading 'integration'). This occurs when a booking has no destination calendar and the location is set to MeetLocationType.

[Medium] Potential N+1 DB query in createAllCalendarEvents for multiple destination calendars

The createAllCalendarEvents method now iterates over event.destinationCalendar array. For each destination calendar where credentialId is set but the credential is not found in the in-memory calendarCredentials array, it performs a separate DB query (prisma.credential.findUnique). This creates an N+1 query pattern where N is the number of destination calendars with uncached credentials. While the number of destination calendars per event is typically small (1-2), this could become a bottleneck if events have many hosts with different calendar credentials.

[High] Potential null dereference on mainHostDestinationCalendar when destinationCalendar is empty array

In the `create` method, the code destructures the first element of `evt.destinationCalendar ?? []` into `mainHostDestinationCalendar`. If `destinationCalendar` is an empty array `[]`, `mainHostDestinationCalendar` will be `undefined`. The subsequent check `mainHostDestinationCalendar.integration !== "google_calendar"` will throw a TypeError because it tries to access `.integration` on `undefined`. This occurs when a user has no destination calendar configured but selects Google Meet as their location.

[Medium] Potential N+1 credential fetch in createAllCalendarEvents when iterating multiple destination calendars

The createAllCalendarEvents method iterates over event.destinationCalendar array. For each destination calendar where credentialId is set but the credential is not found in this.calendarCredentials cache, it performs a separate database query (prisma.credential.findUnique). If destinationCalendar now contains multiple entries (e.g., for multiple hosts), this could result in multiple sequential DB queries per event creation. Previously with a single destination calendar, this was at most one DB query. At scale with many hosts or many events being created concurrently, this could become a bottleneck.

[High] Missing credential ownership validation when fetching from database

In `createAllCalendarEvents`, when a destination calendar's credential is not found in the cached `this.calendarCredentials` list, the code fetches the credential from the database using `prisma.credential.findUnique` without verifying that the credential belongs to the current user or team. This allows an attacker who can control the `destinationCalendar` array (e.g., via booking creation or modification) to specify arbitrary `credentialId` values, potentially using other users' calendar credentials to create events on their calendars.

[High] Null dereference when destinationCalendar is null or empty array

After destructuring `evt.destinationCalendar ?? []`, the code accesses `mainHostDestinationCalendar.integration` without checking if `mainHostDestinationCalendar` is undefined. If `destinationCalendar` is null or an empty array, `mainHostDestinationCalendar` will be `undefined`, causing a TypeError: 'Cannot read properties of undefined (reading 'integration')'.

[High] Team destination calendars silently dropped when no primary destination calendar exists

When `evt.destinationCalendar` is `null` (which happens when neither `eventType.destinationCalendar` nor `organizerUser.destinationCalendar` exists), the optional chaining `?.` on line 1068 prevents the push of team destination calendars. This means for collective team events where the organizer has no destination calendar but team members do, the team members' destination calendars are silently ignored, potentially causing booking creation to fail or use wrong calendars.

[High] Unresolved import

The import `@prisma/client` cannot be resolved. @prisma/client not declared in package.json

[High] updateEvent: fallback calendar selection always returns undefined when externalCalendarId is not provided

In updateEvent, when externalCalendarId is falsy (undefined/null/empty), the code tries to find a destination calendar where `cal.externalId === externalCalendarId`. Since externalCalendarId is undefined, this looks for calendars with undefined externalId, which will never match. The result is that selectedCalendar becomes undefined, and the Google Calendar API call will fail with an invalid calendarId. Previously, the code used `event.destinationCalendar?.externalId` which worked because destinationCalendar was a single object. Now that it's an array, the fallback logic is broken.

[High] deleteEvent: fallback calendar selection always returns undefined when externalCalendarId is not provided

Same bug as in updateEvent. In deleteEvent, when externalCalendarId is not provided, the fallback logic `event.destinationCalendar?.find((cal) => cal.externalId === externalCalendarId)?.externalId` will always return undefined because it searches for calendars with undefined externalId. This causes the Google Calendar API delete call to fail.

[Medium] createEvent signature change adds required parameter without updating all callers

The createEvent function signature changed from `(calEventRaw: CalendarEvent)` to `(calEventRaw: CalendarEvent, credentialId: number)`, adding a required second parameter. If any caller directly invokes GoogleCalendarService.createEvent with only one argument (as was previously valid), the function will receive undefined for credentialId. The find operation `calEventRaw.destinationCalendar?.find((cal) => cal.credentialId === credentialId)` will then look for calendars with undefined credentialId, which will never match, causing the fallback to 'primary' calendar. This may silently use the wrong calendar.

[Medium] Inverted billing logic for organization slug creation

The diff inverts the conditional logic for setting organization slug and requestedSlug. Previously, when IS_TEAM_BILLING_ENABLED was false, slug was set directly on the organization. When true, slug was not set directly but stored as requestedSlug in metadata (presumably for approval after payment). The new logic does the opposite: when billing is enabled, slug is set directly AND stored as requestedSlug. When billing is disabled, no slug is set at all. This could allow organizations to bypass slug approval when billing is enabled, or prevent organizations from getting a slug when billing is not enabled.

[High] Incorrect handling of destinationCalendar as array

The PR description states destinationCalendar is now an array, but the code still treats it as a single object. The expression `booking.destinationCalendar || user.destinationCalendar` uses logical OR for fallback, which is incorrect when both values are arrays. If `booking.destinationCalendar` is an empty array `[]`, it's truthy, so the fallback to `user.destinationCalendar` never occurs. If `booking.destinationCalendar` is undefined, the fallback to `user.destinationCalendar` works, but then `selectedDestinationCalendar` could be an array (if user.destinationCalendar is an array) or undefined. Then `[selectedDestinationCalendar]` wraps the result in another array, creating a nested array `[[...]]` instead of a flat array. This causes downstream code that expects a flat array of destination calendars to receive incorrect data.

[Medium] Calendar.createEvent interface adds credentialId parameter without ownership enforcement

The `Calendar.createEvent` interface now requires a `credentialId` parameter, but the interface definition does not specify any ownership or authorization requirements. Callers can pass arbitrary credential IDs, and implementations may use these credentials without verifying they belong to the authenticated user. This is a design-level security concern that could lead to unauthorized calendar access.

The constructor parameter type changed from `InsightsBookingServiceOptions` (which was validated by Zod schema) to `InsightsBookingServicePublicOptions` (a plain TypeScript type). golden_comments.comment: Asynchronous functions deleteScheduledEmailReminder and deleteScheduledSMSReminder are called without await inside forEach loops. This occurs during booking rescheduling/cancellation, and workflow/workflow step deletion/updates. Consequently, scheduled workflow reminders may not be reliably cancelled, potentially leaving them active.

When immediateDelete is true, the deleteScheduledEmailReminder function cancels the SendGrid email but fails to delete the corresponding WorkflowReminder record from the database. This creates orphaned database entries and is inconsistent with the immediateDelete: false path, which marks the record as cancelled. The SendGrid DELETE API call is also omitted in this path.

https://github.com/calcom/cal.com/pull/8.pr_title: Advanced date override handling and timezone compatibility improvements

golden_comments.comment: Incorrect end time calculation using slotStartTime instead of slotEndTime

Using === for dayjs object comparison will always return false as it compares object references, not values. Use .isSame() method instead: dayjs(date.start).add(utcOffset, 'minutes').isSame(dayjs(date.end).add(utcOffset, minutes))

review_comments.body:
[High] Date override check bypasses busy time validation

When a date override exists for a slot, the `checkIfIsAvailable` function returns `true` immediately without checking if the user has conflicting bookings during that time. This means users with date overrides will show as available even when they have overlapping bookings, leading to double-booking.

[Medium] O(n) dateOverrides scan inside checkIfIsAvailable called per slot

The checkIfIsAvailable function now iterates over all dateOverrides for every time slot. This adds O(dateOverrides) work per slot. With 100 date overrides and 1000 slots, this adds 100,000 extra iterations. Each iteration creates multiple dayjs objects and performs timezone calculations. The utcOffset calculation is recomputed for every override on every slot, even though it only depends on the date and organizerTimeZone which are constant per slot.

[Medium] O(n) workingHours scan inside checkIfIsAvailable called per slot

After checking dateOverrides, checkIfIsAvailable also scans all workingHours for every slot. This adds O(workingHours) work per slot. With 7 working hours and 1000 slots, this adds 7,000 extra iterations. The workingHours.find() creates a new function scope and performs day-of-week and time comparisons for each working hour.

https://github.com/calcom/cal.com/pull/1.pr_title: SMS workflow reminder retry count tracking

golden_comments.comment: Using retryCount: reminder.retryCount + 1 reads a possibly stale value and can lose increments under concurrency; consider an atomic increment via Prisma (increment: 1) to avoid race conditions (also applies to the similar update in the catch block).

The deletion logic in scheduleSMSReminders.ts incorrectly deletes non-SMS workflow reminders (e.g., Email, WhatsApp) that have retryCount > 1. This occurs because the retryCount condition within the OR clause for deletion lacks a method: WorkflowMethods.SMS filter, causing it to apply to all reminder types instead of only SMS reminders, which is the intended scope of this function.

review_comments.body:
[Medium] Overly broad deletion condition may delete non-SMS reminders

The deleteMany query now includes an OR condition that deletes ALL workflow reminders with retryCount > 1, regardless of their method (SMS, EMAIL, etc.) or scheduled date. This means if an attacker can cause retryCount to exceed 1 on any reminder (e.g., by providing invalid phone numbers that cause SMS failures), that reminder will be deleted even if it's for a different notification method or has a future scheduled date. The original query only deleted SMS reminders past their scheduled date.

[High] retryCount not reset on successful SMS send

When an SMS sends successfully (the if branch at line 175), the code updates the reminder with the referenceId but does NOT reset retryCount to 0. This means if a reminder previously failed (retryCount incremented to 1), then succeeded, then failed again later, the retryCount would be 2 instead of 1, causing premature deletion. The retryCount should be reset to 0 on successful send to ensure it only counts consecutive failures.
